lipid peroxidations products (malondialdehyde and d-ROMs) are significantly correlated with circulating triglyceride levels, but not with circulating cholesterol levels.
lipid peroxidations are a good marker of lipid peroxidation but that the levels of lipid peroxidations in blood are related to the concentration of circulating lipids.
lipid peroxidations markers covary positively with circulating lipid levels, and that this relationship explains a considerable amount of their variance in several species.

the potential confounding effect of lipid concentration on measures of oxidative stress.
the confounding effects of lipid concentration in measures of oxidative damage and the potential causes and consequences of this confounding effect.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in birds at least, circulating triglyceride levels are a good predictor of lipid peroxidation, but cholesterol levels are not.
the relationship between lipid peroxidation and circulating triglycerides is species specific and that, at least in birds, it is not a general phenomenon.
the relationship between lipid concentration and lipid peroxidation is species dependent, and it is not possible to generalize it to all species.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipid peroxidative markers should not be used as absolute markers of oxidative stress in the absence of information on circulating lipid levels.
the lipid concentration in the blood should be taken into consideration in order to properly interpret the information given by lipid peroxidation products.
the use of lipid peroxidation products as biomarkers of oxidative stress should be accompanied with a proper correction for lipid concentration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, when using lipid peroxidations markers, it is crucial to control for circulating lipid levels.
the use of lipid peroxidation products as markers of oxidative stress in the organism requires the consideration of circulating lipids as a potential confounding factor.
